explanation: Olympia's temple held Phidias's gold and ivory statue of Zeus, one of the Seven Wonders. Other festivals honoured other gods: Apollo at Delphi, Poseidon at Corinth.

claims.text: The ancient Olympic Games at Olympia were held in honour of Zeus.
The ancient Olympic Games did not honour Apollo, Poseidon or Athena, who were honoured at the Pythian Games, the Isthmian Games and the Panathenaic Games.
The Statue of Zeus at Olympia, made by Phidias in gold and ivory, was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
The Pythian Games at Delphi honoured Apollo, and the Isthmian Games near Corinth honoured Poseidon.

evidence.restatement: The Olympic festival at Olympia was a religious festival for Zeus, whose sanctuary and great temple stood there.
Apollo was honoured at the Pythian Games at Delphi, Poseidon at the Isthmian Games near Corinth and Athena at the Panathenaia in Athens; the Olympics were for Zeus.
Phidias made the seated chryselephantine (gold and ivory) Zeus for the temple at Olympia, and it is one of the classic Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

evidence.restatement: The Pythian Games at Delphi were held for Apollo and the Isthmian Games at the Isthmus of Corinth for Poseidon.
The ancient Olympic festival at Olympia was dedicated to Zeus, whose temple there housed his great cult statue.

claimResults.note: Rival test: Athena, Apollo and Poseidon each had their own festival (Panathenaic, Pythian, Isthmian), so Zeus is the only one of the four tied to Olympia.

evidence.restatement: Apollo's festival was the Pythian Games at Delphi, Poseidon's the Isthmian Games near Corinth and Athena's the Panathenaic Games at Athens.
Phidias made the seated gold-and-ivory statue of Zeus at Olympia around 435 BC, and it appears on the usual list of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
The Pythian Games at Delphi honoured Apollo and the Isthmian Games on the Isthmus of Corinth honoured Poseidon.
